headline: Expelled four students after disciplinary hearings; approved opioid grant and four policies; BDE policy failed.
summary: Staff reported on math and reading growth, attendance, and student clubs, and a resident spoke about policy BCA-R. Personnel changes, including coaching hires, resignations, and transfers, were listed on the consent agenda. The minutes identify students only by letter.
decisions: Approved submitting an opioid grant application, 5-0.
Approved the second reading of policies BCA-R, BCB, BCC, and BDE-R, 5-0.
Motion to approve the second reading of policy BDE failed 4-1, because it needed five votes.

PUBLIC INPUT 
Andrew Jones commented on policy BCA-R prior meeting conversation. Feels it is political in nature. Effort to 
chill free speech. Shared example about point of order and his take on consequences/interactions. 
 
SCHOOL REPORTS 
Jon Radtke presented on data growth in Math and Reading noting the bottom quartile. 87% attendance over 80% 
last year. Too many student tardies. We’re completely staffed.
MINUTES – LEWISTON SCHOOL COMMITTEE MEETING HELD NOVEMBER 2, 2026 – PAGE 3 
 
Deb Rodrigue presented on interventions and MTSS. The 21st Century clubs offer opportunities for belonging 
and building partnerships with families. Attendance is better and instruction is improving. Special Olympics is 
coming to introduce inclusive play. The Sandy Hook implementation has been a success. 
 
Cindy Gish presented on belonging efforts and clubs growing, NWEA goals in Math and Reading. Attendance is 
improving. Professional development and adult care are strong. We started Big Brother & Big Sister with Bates 
this year. It is a multi-year program. Through MTSS we have a PIP (positive impact person). We have staff 
willing to be that person. 
 
OPIOID GRANT 
 Jenny Darigan presented.  
VOTED: (1) Motion to approve submission of grant application. 
Luke Jensen – Elizabeth Eames. (5-0) 
 
POLICIES 
Assistant Superintendent Karen Paquette presented. 
VOTED: (2) Motion to approve the 2nd read of the following policies:  
Luke Jensen – Julia Harper. (5-0)  
a. BCA-R - School Committee Concern Procedure 
b. BCB -School Committee Member Conflict of Interest  
c. BCC -Nepotism 
e. BDE-R Standing Committee Operating Procedures 
 
VOTED: (3) Motion to approve the 2nd read of the following policy:  
Scott Harriman – Julie Harper. (4-1) L. Jensen. Motion fails due to needing 5 votes. 
d. BDE - School Committee Standing Committees

 None. 
 
REPORT FROM SCHOOL SUPERINTENDENT 
Superintendent Jake Langlais reported on the election. Legislative efforts are underway. The survey 
rule/guidance changes federally. 
 
REPORT FROM CITY COUNCIL REP 
 The City Council met last week. Work on the mobile home rent stabilization ordinance is going in a slightly 
 different direction. 
 
UPDATES FROM SCHOOL COMMITTEE SUBCOMMITTEES 
 None 
 
SCHOOL COMMITTEE COMMUNITY ANNOUNCEMENTS 
 4 student reps are trained to be School Committee representatives. 
 
FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS 
 None.
